name: asr-whisper-helpline-sw-v1
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from openai/whisper-large-v2 (config.json max_position_embeddings 1500). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-06. A two-stage Swahili ASR fine-tune of openai/whisper-large-v2 for Tanzania Child Helpline telephony, not a new base model: 1.543B tensor set (config inherited: 32 layers, 1280 hidden, 20 KV heads). Stage 1 streamed Common Voice 17.0 sw for 10k steps at lr 1e-5; stage 2 continued on CV 23.0 for 7.5k steps at lr 5e-6, best validation WER 23.56% at step 7,500 and the weights restored to that checkpoint. Recorded because the card's comparison table prints the base's zero-shot 89.05% next to this model's 23.62% on the same CV 17.0 validation split. TWO CAVEATS, both kept in the benchmark configs: the released weights are the stage-2 checkpoint while the 23.62% cell belongs to stage 1, and neither model has been measured on the telephony audio the model is actually for. Licence apache-2.0, repo created 2025-09-10.

benchmarks.name: Common Voice 17.0 Swahili validation WER (stage 1)
benchmarks.config: Card 'Performance Comparison' table: '| Whisper Large v2 (baseline) | CV 17.0 | Validation | 89.05% |' vs '| This model (Stage 1) | CV 17.0 | Validation | 23.62% |'. Same split, same metric; base is zero-shot. Lower is better. CAVEAT: the card attributes 23.62% to the stage-1 checkpoint, while the weights in this repo are the stage-2 best checkpoint (early-stopped at step 7,500 of stage 2). The stage-1 and stage-2 numbers are close (23.62 vs 23.56) but they are not the same weights, and the card never evaluates the released checkpoint on CV 17.0.

benchmarks.name: Common Voice 23.0 Swahili validation WER (stage-2 best checkpoint)
benchmarks.config: Card stage-2 results: best checkpoint at step 7,500, validation WER 23.5627%. No base column exists on this split - the 89.05% baseline is on CV 17.0 - so this row is the model's own absolute score, not a same-table comparison.
